title: Interactive ring tool: hover to preview a loop on the surface, click to confirm and tighten
description:
User ruling 2026-09-06: typing coordinates into the terminal is not an acceptable way to author a ring. Build a mouse tool in the mesh-viewer / quad-layout scenes (on ModelScene so every model scene gets it): a keybind (R) starts the tool; while it is active, moving the mouse over the surface shows a preview loop through the point under the cursor, updating every frame; a left click confirms the previewed loop, tightens it with FlipOut (SurfaceRing from CRAW-23), adds it to the scene's rings, appends its loop_through_points statement to the working .dsl (RingDslWriter) using waypoints sampled from the confirmed loop such that re-evaluation reproduces the ring element-exact; Escape leaves the tool keeping every confirmed ring; Enter also confirms. Pieces: (1) picking: a SurfacePicker on ModelScene that returns face id, barycentric hit and world point under the cursor; implement as GPU face-id picking (render face index to an offscreen id buffer, read one pixel) so it is O(1) per frame on the 936k-face scan; no CPU brute force; this is the picking CRAW-7 needs, so CRAW-7 reuses it. (2) preview loop: the plane through the hit point whose normal is the local limb axis: the tangent of the nearest skeleton branch sample when a skeleton is available (MeshSkeletonExtractor, computed once per model and cached), otherwise the minimum-curvature principal direction averaged over a small neighbourhood (PrincipalDirectionField), which is the tube axis on any limb; the loop is the plane-surface intersection walked from the hit face (BranchCrossSectionRing's face walk from CRAW-22), so it costs milliseconds and needs no tightening for the preview. Scroll wheel while active tilts the plane about the view axis; Shift+scroll about the other tangent, for the cases where the estimated axis is wrong. (3) rendering: rings must be unmistakable. Add thick ring rendering to HalfEdgeMeshRuntime: extrude each ring polyline into a screen-facing strip (or thin tube) of a fixed pixel width, depth-biased so it sits on the surface, distinct colour per ring, the ring's number drawn at its centroid; the preview loop in a fourth colour. Route every existing ring overlay through it (CRAW-22 ring_NN labels, CRAW-23 ring_seed / ring_tightened) and remove the 1-px feature-edge path for rings; the STAGES-mode-only gating goes away, rings draw in every shader mode. (4) status line: while the tool is active the scene HUD shows 'ring tool: hover to preview, click to confirm, scroll to tilt, Esc to finish' and after a confirm the ring row (edges, length, centroid). (5) automation: /input routes already inject mouse moves and clicks; add a ring-tool state to ui-state (active, preview edge count, confirmed rings) so run-scene can drive and screenshot it.

Consolidation 2026-09-06: the user will not merge CRAW-22 or CRAW-23 until the interactive tool works end to end, so all three are built in one worktree, /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/.claude/worktrees/craw-rings (branch craw-rings on master c3e0794c), by one agent; CRAW-22 and CRAW-23 diffs were applied there mechanically with three patch rejects left for the agent to resolve.

Ruling 2026-09-06 after user testing: the preview is correct but confirm let FlipOut slide the loop to the nearest neck, so the ring was not where the user clicked. Confirm must pin the clicked point: treat the loop as an open path from the picked vertex back to itself with fixed endpoints, straightening everything except the pin; render the pin as a marker both while hovering and on the confirmed ring; loop_through_points gains pin=true so the written statement reloads element-exact. Adding, moving and removing pins on an existing ring is CRAW-30.

Redesign 2026-09-07 (user testing showed pinned FlipOut rings become polygons of geodesics with corners at the pins): a ring is a closed cubic spline on the surface through anchor points, traced with b/Surf's recursive de Casteljau by geodesic midpoints (Mancinelli, Nazzaro, Pellacini, Puppo 2021; paper at ~/QuadLayoutsPapersToRead/MNP*21, code github.com/Claudiomancinelli90/B-Surf), each geodesic between two surface points coming from the existing FlipOut port. Hover: the girth preview under the cursor is fitted with anchors (start with 4 evenly spaced, trace, insert an anchor at the largest deviation, repeat until every point is within max(5 percent of the loop's mean radius, one local edge length)); the anchor count shows live. Confirm stores the anchors; the ring is the spline through them, snapped to a conforming edge cycle by ConformingLoopSnap, drawn thick and numbered with a dot per anchor. Clicking an existing ring inserts an anchor at the nearest spline point and re-traces its two neighbouring segments (smooth, no corner). New node spline_ring(geometry, points) so the saved statement re-traces the same ring; loop_through_points keeps the geodesic chain for the automatic candidates and the terminal path. The pinned confirm path is removed from the tool; FlipGeodesics.vertexIsPinned and loop_through_points pin=true stay as the mechanism for a later explicit 'tighten to the neck holding these anchors' edit (CRAW-30).
definition-of-done: 1. Launch entry 'CRAW-28: Ring Tool (fertility)': F5 shows the five automatic rings thick and numbered; R, hover mid-thigh: a smooth ring previews under the cursor with its anchors drawn and their count in the HUD; click: the ring is placed where the preview was (centroid within 5 percent of the mean radius of the preview's centroid, no corner: every interior angle of the traced polyline above 150 degrees), numbered 6; click on ring 6 elsewhere: an anchor is inserted there and the ring passes through it smoothly; Esc keeps everything. Screenshots of each step under tmp/, driven through the /input routes on port 47869. 2. Same on the crawfish (repaired via CRAW-26's repair_mesh, now on master): hover a claw arm and a tail segment, preview under 16 ms per frame including the anchor fit, confirm both. 3. Each confirmed ring's spline_ring statement is appended to the working .dsl and reloads element-exact (fingerprint equality). 4. Anchor fitting: on a procedural straight tube 4 anchors suffice; on a procedural tapered tube more are inserted and the fitted spline stays within tolerance of the cross-section (unit tests, no mesh files). 5. Unit: spline through 4 anchors on a procedural sphere reproduces a great circle within 0.5 percent of its length; inserting an anchor off the circle bends the curve through it with no interior angle below 150 degrees. 6. Every ring overlay (automatic, spline, terminal) draws through the thick numbered renderer in every shader mode. 7. Build checkstyle-green; unit tests load no mesh files.
testing-plan: 1. Procedural unit tests: sphere great circle, straight and tapered tubes, anchor insertion smoothness. 2. run-scene on fertility driving R/hover/click/click-on-ring/Esc through the input routes, screenshots, .dsl reload fingerprints. 3. Same on the repaired crawfish with frame timing.

Ruling wanted: the crawfish hover fit measures 13 to 29 ms per frame, over the 16 ms the DoD asks for
unknowns: How many waypoints sampled from a confirmed loop are needed for loop_through_points to reproduce it element-exact on re-evaluation (3 may not suffice on a twisted limb; measure)
Whether the min-curvature fallback is stable enough near junctions or should be replaced by the skeleton always (skeleton cost on the scan is seconds; cache per model)
Whether Escape should also confirm the current preview (user said 'escape or clicking confirms'); implemented as click/Enter confirm, Escape finish-keeping-confirmed; verify with the user

ANSWERED (waypoint count): on the fertility leg 3 waypoints sampled from the tightened loop reproduce it element-exact. On the small child's-arm ring no sampling of the tightened loop (3, 6, 12 or 24 points) reproduces it - every count converges to a neighbouring geodesic - so the tool falls back to the 3 waypoints of the preview cut it was built from, which reproduce it by construction, and says so in the HUD. Both crawfish rings took the same fallback. The written statement is therefore always element-exact; the ladder only decides whether the waypoints come from the tightened loop (preferred, transfers better under CRAW-24) or from the preview

ANSWERED (axis estimate): neither named estimate is usable on its own. On fertility the TEASAR skeleton at resolution 128 is 22 branches / 58 joints, all fanning from one limb tip, so the nearest-segment tangent pointed along -X everywhere on the leg and the cut ran the length of the limb; the min-curvature fallback was no better near junctions. The plane is now FOUND rather than estimated: a girdling normal must lie in the surface tangent plane at the hit, so GirdlingPlane scans that one angle and keeps the shortest closed cut, with the skeleton or curvature estimate only choosing where the scan starts. RULING NEEDED: this is a deviation from the ticket's wording, which says the normal IS the limb axis

RULING NEEDED (Escape): implemented as click/Enter confirm, Escape finish-keeping-every-confirmed-ring, and Escape no longer opens the model menu while the tool is running. The user's 'escape or clicking confirms' would instead make Escape confirm the hovered loop and then leave; say which

RULING NEEDED (ring numbering): the on-screen thick rings are numbered from 1 in overlay order, so the CRAW-22 fixture reads 1..5 and the first confirmed ring is 6, matching the DoD wording. PatchRenderer's Set-of-Mark multiview still numbers the same rings from 0. One of the two should change

The girdling search finds no closed cut at some hover points on the crawfish shell, because that shell is an open surface (the scan's missing back is a boundary) and a plane cut that reaches the hole cannot close. CRAW-26's repair should remove most of these; the tool simply shows no preview there

RULING NEEDED (how many pins a confirm makes): the ticket's ruling says to pin only the clicked point and let everything else straighten. Measured on the fertility thigh, that is not enough. One pin gave a ring of 38 edges, length 84.46985, centroid -60.34449,-25.74061,1.32490 - only 3.5 from the automatic neck ring's centroid and visibly not where the click was: FlipOut tilts the loop obliquely down the taper, keeping only the pinned point in place (its waypoints span x -47 to -72). Pinning the three points of the previewed cut instead keeps the ring on the preview: 42 edges, length 88.90398, centroid 10.56 from the neck ring. Shipped as three pins (RingTool.PIN_WAYPOINTS), so the confirmed ring has three kinks rather than one. Say whether that is the wanted behaviour or whether one pin plus something else (a tilt lock, a length cap) should hold the ring instead

ANSWERED (waypoints for an element-exact reload, under pinning): three, always. Pinning makes the written statement self-defining - the waypoints are the pins that determine the ring - so the reload recomputes the same ring by construction instead of having to search a 3/6/12/24 ladder for a sampling that happens to converge to the same geodesic. Verified live: fingerprint fd516a968eb12c65 both from the tool and from re-evaluating the appended statement

The pin is always a mesh vertex: the corner of the picked face nearest the barycentric hit. On the fertility thigh the click sat 0.49 local edge lengths from the vertex it pinned, so a ring can land up to half an edge from where the user aimed; RingTool logs when that fraction passes 0.5 and ui-state reports it as pinSnapFraction. Splitting the face to put the pin exactly under the cursor is CRAW-30 territory and was not done

A confirmed ring's pin is drawn in the ring's own colour, as the ticket asks, which makes it a bead on a band rather than a contrasting dot; it reads only because the disc is 10 px against the ribbon's 4 px half-width. If pins should stand out against their ring, they need a second colour or a rim

Driving the tool through /input: a click confirms the loop the LAST RENDERED FRAME previewed, not the loop under the coordinates the click carries, because the click handler runs before the next perFrame. An agent script must hover, wait a frame, then click the same point; clicking straight at a new point confirms the previous hover's ring. Worth making the click re-pick before confirming

MEASURED, DoD item 2 NOT MET: the hover fit does not fit 16 ms on the 938302-face crawfish. Per frame, including the GPU pick, the girdling search and the whole anchor fit: 13.1 ms on a 62-edge cut (4 anchors, 32 geodesics), 24.7 ms on a 320-edge cut (9 anchors, 486 geodesics), 28.6 ms on a 563-edge cut (7 anchors, 352 geodesics), and 19 to 75 ms at points where the girdling search finds no closed cut and spends the frame failing. Fertility (27954 faces) is 1.7 to 4.9 ms. Two rounds of optimisation are already in: the fit re-measures only the four segments an insertion re-traced (a 320-edge cut went from 873 geodesics to 486), and hover traces one bisection shallower than a confirm. The remaining cost is about 60 microseconds per geodesic, of which the A* seed over 469131 vertices is most; the levers left are a smaller maximumDepth on hover, a coarser tolerance, or restricting the triangulation to a band around the cut. RULING NEEDED: accept the measured rate, or spend another pass on it

DoD item 2 says 'hover a claw arm and a tail segment'. Scan IMG_4109 is the claws and the carapace - there is no tail in it - so the two rings confirmed are the small claw's arm and the big claw. A tail ring needs a member that has one

The sharpest interior angle is above 150 degrees where the DoD measures it (fertility: 160.2) but not on the crawfish scan (139.4 and 149.6 on the two confirmed rings). The scan's surface is tubercled at the scale of a leaf, and consecutive leaves of the RDC are only approximately pieces of one cubic - the geodesic midpoint of two control points is not the 3D chord midpoint, and the gap grows with surface curvature. Deeper bisection does not help: below one mean edge per leaf the control points can no longer be placed apart. Say whether the 150-degree floor should hold on a raw scan too

dsl/fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl had 15 loop_through_points statements left behind by the previous session's tool runs again, so it drew 20 rings instead of the five DoD item 1 asks for. Trimmed back to load_mesh + ring_candidates and restored to that after every run. The tool writes to src/main/resources while the scene loads from target/classes, so a reload check has to copy the file across; worth making workingDslPath and the loader agree

Ring numbering after a reload is the iteration order of the edge-marks map, not the order the rings were authored, so the confirmed ring drew as 6 live and as 4 after reload. The live numbering is what DoD item 1 asks for; the reloaded numbering should probably follow the statement order
changes-made: SurfacePicker (geometry/mesh/data/paths): Moller-Trumbore ray/face hit giving the face id, the three barycentric weights and the world point; the tool narrows the ray to one face with the GPU id buffer first, and only the unit test scans every face

GPU face-id picking in HalfEdgeMeshRuntime: uploadPickBuffer builds an unwelded draw whose every corner carries its face index split across three colour bytes (mesh_pick.vs/.fs, ShaderType.MeshPick); pickFaceIndexAt renders it into a ONE-PIXEL viewport with a gluPickMatrix-style projection so only the cursor's fragment rasterizes, reads that pixel, and restores the cleared frame. 464 ms to build on the 920091-face crawfish shell, O(1) per frame after; pickRay unprojects the same pixel for the exact barycentric hit

PlaneSurfaceLoop (paths): the plane/surface intersection walked face by face with crossings computed only on the faces touched, plus a maximumLength budget that abandons a cut running along a limb. CRAW-22's BranchCrossSectionRing lost its duplicate walk and calls it

GirdlingPlane (paths): the preview plane. A girdling normal lies in the surface's tangent plane at the hit, so the search is one angle: 12 scan directions across the half-circle seeded by the LimbAxis estimate, 3 bisection rounds, shortest closed cut wins, each walk budgeted by the best so far. Scroll tilt is applied to the winner

LimbAxis (geometry/mesh/data): the two estimates the ticket names, cached per model - the tangent of the nearest skeleton SEGMENT (samples are RDP-simplified tens of units apart, so nearest-joint named the wrong limb) and the PrincipalDirectionField minimum-curvature direction averaged over the hit face's one-ring. Both are seeds for the search rather than the answer

RingTool (scenes/model) on ModelScene: R starts it, every frame picks the face under the cursor and cuts the girdling plane, left click or Enter tightens with SurfaceRing/FlipOut into a numbered ring and appends its loop_through_points statement, Escape finishes keeping every confirmed ring. OrbitMouseTrap gained toolClick/toolScroll hooks so the click confirms and the wheel tilts only while the tool runs; KeyGuy.shiftMask is public so Shift+scroll picks the other tilt axis

Thick ring rendering in HalfEdgeMeshRuntime: setRingOverlay takes packed segments per ring and draws each as a screen-facing ribbon of fixed pixel half-width (4 px), depth-biased onto the surface, one colour per ring, with the ring's number projected at its length-weighted centroid and drawn by the scene's font. Every ring overlay goes through it - CRAW-22's ring_NN, CRAW-23's ring_seed/ring_tightened, select_ring's selected_ring, the confirmed rings and the preview - in every shader mode; the 1-px feature-edge path for rings and the STAGES-only gating are gone

ui-state gained a ringTool block (active, preview validity/edge count/length/ms, tilt angles, waypointsPerRing, hit point, plane normal, limb axis, confirmed ring rows with fingerprints, the drawn ring labels and colours) and the scene HUD shows the status line, the live preview row and the last confirmed ring row

MeshNodeViewerScene.workingDslPath now returns null when the viewer is showing a mesh file rather than its own graph; without that the tool appended ring statements to skull.dsl while the crawfish OBJ was on screen

Launch entry 'CRAW-28: Ring Tool (fertility)' beside the CRAW-22 and CRAW-23 ones; unit test unit.mesh.SurfacePickerTest (procedural cube: face, weights that interpolate the hit, and a miss; procedural 48x40 tube: the girdling normal is 0.13 degrees off the tube axis and the cut is its circumference)

Fertility, driven through /input on port 47869: five ring_NN loops draw thick and numbered on load with no key press; R + hover at the leg previews 77 edges / 82.358 long at 2.4 ms per frame; the click tightens it to 41 edges / 81.88591, centroid -61.63545,-22.49287,1.24272, fingerprint 977890025bbaba86 - element-identical to CRAW-22's automatic ring_01; Esc keeps it. Screenshots tmp/craw28_fertility_{rings_on_load,hover_preview,confirmed_ring,after_esc,reloaded_dsl}.png

Element-exact reload: the two statements the tool appended to dsl/fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl re-evaluate to fingerprints 977890025bbaba86 and 358ead1528204e36, equal to the live rings' (the fixture was restored afterwards, so the deliverable diff does not carry them)

Crawfish, on the 920091-face largest manifold shell (repair_mesh is not on master; exported by FlipGeodesicsScanBenchmark -Dbenchmark.shellObj): preview 6.7 to 9.5 ms per frame over seven hover points, well inside the 16 ms target; a claw-arm ring confirms at 73 edges / 0.11760 (fingerprint 72c3f4cedd25e046) and a tail-segment ring at 271 edges / 0.43814 (a3355a3ecd25232d). Screenshots tmp/craw28_crawfish_{load,hover_claw,hover_tail,confirmed}.png, log tmp/craw28_crawfish_scene.log

Rings draw thick and numbered in LAMBERT, FLAT, STAGES, CREST_VS_BOUNDARY and SCALAR (screenshots tmp/craw28_fertility_shader_1..4.png); dsl/fixtures/torus_loop_through_points.dsl and fertility_ring_pick.dsl both still validate, the latter now drawing selected_ring thick as a sixth ring

Pinned confirm (CRAW-28 ruling): FlipGeodesics gained a public boolean[] vertexIsPinned; a wedge whose apex is a pinned intrinsic vertex is never enqueued, so the path keeps its corner there while every other corner straightens. This is the fixed-endpoint mode the ruling asks for, expressed on a closed loop instead of an open path duplicated at its ends, and it is the same machinery CRAW-30's multi-pin rings need

SurfaceRing.through / tightenedOrNull gained a 'pinned' count: how many leading waypoints the tightening must keep the ring on. 0 is the old free loop (ring_candidates, ring_at_branch, the terminal ring command and the /mesh/rings/add route all pass 0 and are unchanged); the ring tool passes every waypoint. SurfaceRing also exposes pathVertexIds, the mesh vertices the tightened path turns at

loop_through_points gained a boolean 'pin' input, default false = today's behaviour. true holds every authored point and only the arcs between consecutive points straighten. socketDocs written; mesh-node-catalog.json regenerates on build. RingDslWriter.append/statement gained the flag and writes pin=true|false

RingTool.confirm no longer hands the loop to a free FlipOut. It picks the corner of the hit face nearest the barycentric hit as the pin, samples PIN_WAYPOINTS=3 points of the previewed cut starting at the pin, snaps each to a vertex, and tightens with all three held. The written statement's waypoints ARE the pins, so the reload is element-exact by construction rather than by a search: the 3/6/12/24 waypoint ladder and its fallback are gone

Pin marker: HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.setRingPins draws one camera-facing disc of fixed pixel radius (10 px, twice the ring ribbon's depth bias) per pin, in that ring's colour - the hovered pin in the preview colour at the cursor, and one on every confirmed ring. Drawn after the ring ribbons in every shader mode

ui-state ringTool gained pin (the hovered pin's position), pinVertexId and pinSnapFraction, and each confirmedRings row gained its own pin; the HUD preview line reads 'pin at x,y,z (N edge lengths from the cursor)' and the confirmed row reads 'pinned at x,y,z'; the status line now says 'click to confirm the loop through the pin'

Fertility on port 47869, driven through /input: hover at (310,500) mid-thigh hits (-47.40325,-22.80316,2.34535) and pins vertex 7775 at (-47.44950,-22.71520,3.47314), 0.49 local edge lengths away; preview 83 edges / 88.6597 long / 1.6 ms per frame. The click confirms 42 edges, length 88.90398, centroid -57.59954,-32.25137,1.12784, fingerprint fd516a968eb12c65, 3 pinned waypoints, 24 ms. The automatic neck ring on that limb (ring_01, measured by rings-list) is length 81.88591 at centroid -61.63545,-22.49287,1.24273: the confirmed ring's centroid is 10.56 away from it, where the old unpinned confirm reproduced it exactly (same 977890025bbaba86 fingerprint). Esc keeps it. Screenshots tmp/craw28_pin_{rings_on_load,hover_preview,confirmed_ring,after_esc,reloaded_dsl}.png

Element-exact reload under pinning: the appended statement ring1 = loop_through_points(..., pin=true, label="ring1") re-evaluates on reload to 42 edges, fingerprint fd516a968eb12c65, equal to the live ring. Three waypoints, always - pinning makes the statement self-defining, so no ladder is needed. The fixture was restored afterwards

LoopThroughPointsTest gained three pinned cases on a procedural tube pinched to half its radius at x=0: the free ring slides to the waist (centroid x 0.066, length 1.284) while the ring pinned at x=1 stays (centroid x 0.988, length 2.429) and keeps every waypoint on the path; the pinned ring reloads element-exact through the node from 3 waypoints; and the writer emits pin=true byte-stably. No mesh file is loaded

dsl/fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl carried nine loop_through_points statements left behind by the previous session's tool runs, so the fixture drew 14 rings instead of the five DoD item 4 asks for. Trimmed back to load_mesh + ring_candidates; it now draws exactly ring_00..ring_04 with no key press

Crawfish, on the 920091-face largest manifold shell, same session: preview 5.7 to 12.6 ms per frame over eleven hover points, inside the 16 ms target. A claw-arm ring confirms pinned at 0.21255,0.02657,0.12896 as 243 edges / 0.42158 (seed 0.44186, fingerprint f40c93a6f3478ee0) and a tail-segment ring pinned at 0.23214,0.04388,-0.21616 as 107 edges / 0.16518 (bc4ec0284d4d38ef); both took 3 pinned waypoints and about 0.8 s, which is the IntrinsicTriangulation build over 920k faces, not the tightening. Screenshots tmp/craw28_pin_crawfish_{load,confirmed}.png. The scene shows a mesh file, so workingDslPath is null and the HUD says the ring was not written, as designed

SurfaceGeodesics (geometry/mesh/data/paths): the geodesic primitives a spline needs, over one IntrinsicTriangulation built per model and kept. A run seeds with an A* walk over mesh edges (b/Surf 5.2, so the cost tracks the distance between the two points, not the mesh size), tightens with FlipOut, traces onto the surface, and then undoes its own flips, so repeating a call returns the same path however many ran in between. Also walkFrom, the straight surface walk the tangent handles are built with

IntrinsicTriangulation gained a flip journal (recordFlips, undoFlips, forgetFlips): every flip saves the six half-edges, the edge, the two faces and the two vertex references it is about to overwrite, and undoFlips replays them value by value, so a cached triangulation returns bit-identical and a later trace is deterministic. FlipGeodesics no longer clears its edge-occupancy array over the whole mesh per run - it tracks the edges it occupied and clears only those, which is what makes hundreds of short tightenings per frame affordable

SurfaceSplineTracer (paths): b/Surf's RDC (Mancinelli et al. 2021, 3.4 and 4.1.1). A cubic segment is bisected at t=1/2 with manifold averages - the midpoint of the FlipOut geodesic between two vertices - recursing to a depth the mesh sets: as deep as keeps a leaf at least one mean edge long (shortestLeafInEdges = 2 by default), capped at maximumDepth. Every control point carries both a mesh vertex and the exact surface point the average landed on, up to half an edge apart. Parallel arrays per segment, no per-segment class

The emitted polyline is the leaf's cubic sampled where the geodesic between its end vertices crosses the mesh, not the geodesic itself. Sampling the geodesic concentrates all the ring's turning at the leaf joins (measured 147.8 degrees on the fertility thigh); sampling the cubic spreads it over every point (160.2 degrees, same anchors, same edge cycle). Each point keeps the vertex/edge correspondence the conforming snap needs, so the edge cycle is unchanged either way

Tangent handles: both handles at an anchor lie on one line through it, so the junction is smooth rather than a corner. The direction is the chord-length-weighted (Barry-Goldman) Catmull-Rom tangent, projected into the surface tangent plane; the length is (4/3)tan(alpha/2)c/(2 sin alpha) for the angle alpha between the tangent and the chord, which makes a cubic reproduce the circular arc through two anchors exactly and degrades to a third of the chord as the segment straightens. Plain Catmull-Rom handles (chord/6) undershoot a great circle by 12 percent

SplineAnchorFit (paths): four anchors spread evenly by arc length over the girdling cut, trace, then one more at the worst deviation until every traced point is inside max(5 percent of the loop's mean radius, one mean edge length), capped at 24 anchors and reported when the cap is hit. Inserting an anchor re-traces only the four segments whose control polygon moved (the two it splits and the two whose end tangent it moved) and re-measures only those, since the untouched segments still hold the very arrays already measured

SurfaceSpline (paths): the value a traced spline publishes - anchors, polyline, the ConformingLoopSnap edge cycle, length, mean radius, centroid, trace depth, and the sharpest interior angle with the point it was measured at. Angles are measured across spans of at least a quarter of a mean edge, so a geodesic grazing a vertex does not read as a corner

spline_ring(geometry, points, label) node with socketDocs; mesh-node-catalog.json regenerates on build. RingDslWriter gained nextRingId, appendSpline and replaceSpline (rewrite one ring's line in place, which an anchor insertion needs so the file stays element-exact); loop_through_points, its pin input and FlipGeodesics.vertexIsPinned are untouched and are what CRAW-30's tighten-to-neck will use

RingTool: the pinned confirm path is gone. Hover picks the face, cuts the girdling plane, fits anchors and traces the spline; a click confirms it, or - when the cursor is within 8 pixels of a confirmed ring - inserts an anchor into that ring and re-traces its neighbouring segments. Hover traces one bisection shallower than a confirm (the fit traces once per anchor it inserts), so a confirm re-traces at full depth before it publishes. HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.setRingPins is setRingAnchors: one 6-px white disc per anchor, in front of the ring ribbon so it reads on any ring colour
